defects.summary: At --std 2002 a communication-section CD field with an implicit description (TEXT LENGTH of an output CD, implicitly PICTURE 9(4)) is modelled with no PICTURE clause, so INVOKE ... RETURNING it and INVOKE ... USING BY REFERENCE it to a PIC 9(4) formal/returning item are refused COBOL0828 as non-conforming.
defects.expected: compiles and prints 5=0042: the implicit description of the output CD is 'equivalent to' a record whose TEXT LENGTH entry is '02 data-name-2 PICTURE 9(4)' (§2002:A.1.2.3 GR16), so the receiving/argument item has the same PICTURE, USAGE and SIGN clauses as the method's PIC 9(4) item (§2002:14.7.2.2, §2002:14.7.1.2.1); identifier-3/identifier-4 may reference a communication-section item (§2002:14.8.22.2 SR9, SR11).
defects.observed: error COBOL0828: INVOKE "GET42" RETURNING 'OTL': the returning item (an elementary numeric item described with PICTURE 9(4) USAGE DISPLAY) and the receiving item (an elementary numeric item described with USAGE DISPLAY) are not described with the same clauses (ISO §2023:14.8.3.3); the BY REFERENCE program gives the same COBOL0828 for USING argument 'OTL'. A CD RECORD item PIC 9(4) (cd-invoke-args.cob, 4=0042) is accepted, so the defect is the implicit-field description. Sibling sweep needed: CALL USING/RETURNING and function arguments with CD implicit fields (MESSAGE COUNT, END KEY, STATUS KEY ...).

defects.summary: At --std 2002 the SELECT WHEN clause is refused (COBOL1705) citing the 2023 optional-element licence Annex A.4.8; 2002 makes SELECT WHEN a required element (only its effect outside CODE-SET/FORMAT processing is optional, B.1 item 139; the FORMAT clause representation is 'required', B.1 item 64). So MERGE GR2 b) and GR13 b) (multiple record descriptions with SELECT WHEN) cannot be exercised at 2002.
defects.expected: compiles at --std 2002 (§2002:13.16.49.2 SR1 permits SELECT WHEN at the 01 level of a file-section record; §2002:14.8.23.3 GR13b applies its rules to select the description that decides the fill); no 2002 text makes it optional.
defects.observed: error COBOL1705: the SELECT WHEN clause on 'GN-NAT' ...: the FORMAT clause (ISO §2023:13.18.24) and the SELECT WHEN clause (ISO §2023:13.18.51) are the two items of Annex A.4.8, an OPTIONAL language element (§2023:4.2.7) for which this implementation claims NO support ... so the clause is refused (identical at --std 2023, where the licence exists). The FORMAT clause at --std 2002 is a sibling to check.

cases.class: other (declined-element reach: the rule's file-name-1 may be an FD with the FORMAT clause, required in 2002 and refused at --std 2002 under the 2023-only licence A.4.8; the 2002 OPEN clause itself names FORMAT-file operands in SR7)
cases.reason: In 2002, OPEN GR1 governs every file connector named in an OPEN, including an FD with the FORMAT clause. 2002 OPEN SR7 restricts only the I-O phrase for such files, so OPEN OUTPUT/INPUT/EXTEND of a FORMAT file is in this clause's 2002 scope. 2002 has no optional licence for FORMAT (3.1.1; 2014 E.2 item 23 lists A.4.7 FORMAT and SELECT WHEN among the features 'required in the previous COBOL standard'). The 2023 CONFORMS rests on A.4.8, under which no FORMAT file exists. Probe: open-format-41.cob is refused COBOL1705 at both 2002 and 2023, while the identical program without FORMAT (open-noformat-control.cob) prints A=00 B=00 C=41 at 2002. needs: a 2002 witness for OPEN of a FORMAT file once FORMAT is supported at --std 2002 (sibling of reader defect D2). compiler-at-2002: wrong (refuses legal 2002 source).

cases.reason: In 2002, GR19 governs every multi-file OPEN, including one that names a FORMAT-clause FD (2002 SR7 shows the OPEN clause covers such operands). Probe open-format-41.cob (OPEN OUTPUT FF FG with FF a FORMAT file) is refused COBOL1705 at 2002. The control without FORMAT runs (A=00 B=00). The RESUME half is covered at 2002 (the reader's probe; RESUME is claimed, A.4.12). needs: a 2002 witness for a multi-file OPEN that includes a FORMAT file. compiler-at-2002: wrong (refuses legal 2002 source).

refute.notes: The cause behind every overturn and doubt is the FORMAT clause. It is required in 2002 (3.1.1; 2014 E.2 item 23), the compiler refuses it at every edition (COBOL1705, A.4.8), and the reader recorded it only as a sibling of D2. Separately, CLASS-ID multiple inheritance (required in 2002, refused COBOL0849) reaches no SAME here as an operand.
